implementerProof.how: The two entries this round changed were re-run here and each was broken on its own. Entry 5 (roll call 5, the new one): `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=2 -run 'TestAFailedFirstStartLogsItsErrorOnlyWhileItIsTheLiveWatch$' ./internal/kvwatch/` passed twice (ok 1.604s), and `go test -run 'TestASilentCutRewatchesTheCachesWithNoErrorLine$' ./cmd/listener/` passed (ok 7.133s, the cut reported 2.833 s in). The entry's own disclosure was checked rather than taken: with the replaced-watch line forced to ERROR in kvwatch.Start, the listener guard still passes (ok 6.332s), so that test does not reach the replaced branch and the unit test is the pin, exactly as the entry says. The entries carried from round 1 were re-run at this head: the listener's silent cut 3 of 3 (2.787 s to 2.856 s for `envoy`, 2.837 s to 2.856 s for `envoy-live-topics`) and the daemon's 2 of 2 under -race (3.011 s and 3.014 s). kvwatch and its three dependants are green under -race (65.755s, 25.581s, 11.697s, 33.249s). Entry 3 (item 1.8) and entry 4 (the suites) were verified in round 1 at code head 725e26a83afa and their code is unchanged since: the diff d5998d5f..d5dbcf92 touches only internal/kvwatch, cmd/listener/cut_rewatch_test.go, one changelog fragment and .legion/.

proof.criterion: Roll call 5, the INFRA-14 architect's decision of 2026-10-30: a watch a rewatch replaced ends without an ERROR line, and a watch that fails while it is still the live one keeps its ERROR.
proof.surface: The kvwatch watcher against a real in-process NATS server, both branches driven directly through its public API (New, Rewatch, Start, KV), with the records read from a JSON logger.
proof.observed: Both rows passed in both runs (ok 1.604s). `no replacement`: the failed first start logs exactly one ERROR `test cache watch failed` and no INFO end line, so a cache nothing feeds still pages. `a rewatch replaced it`: no ERROR record of any message, one INFO `test cache first watch ended because a rewatch replaced it`, and the replacement still delivers a put made afterwards.
proof.negativeControl: Start's old body restored (the unconditional `w.logger().Error(...)` before the lock, the `if !current { w.signalReady() }` after it) with both test files untouched: `--- FAIL ... a first watch a rewatch replaced logged [test cache watch failed: nats: connection closed], want no ERROR`, while the `no replacement` row still passes, so the test separates the two branches rather than counting lines. kvwatch.go was restored with `jj restore` and `jj status` is clean.

proof.criterion: The whole cut path of the real listener writes no ERROR line: a hub that stops answering is declared lost, every cache is rewatched, and the caches follow the bucket again.
proof.surface: The real envoy-listener binary with its three caches and the live topics lane, against an in-process NATS whose relay freezes and thaws, read through its own log and its GET /v1/interests/.
proof.command: From packages/envoy: `go test -count=1 -timeout 15m -v -run 'TestASilentCutRewatchesTheCachesWithNoErrorLine$' ./cmd/listener/`; and a throwaway second-run test of the tester's own (TestTwoSilentCutsInARowRewatchTheCachesWithNoErrorLine), two freezes and two thaws in one process, run the same way and removed afterwards since it pins no defect.
proof.observed: The implementer's guard passed (ok 7.133s), both clients reporting the cut 2.833 s in. The two-cut run passed in 10.86 s: cut 1 reported 2.838 s in and every cache warmed up again 1.062 s after the thaw; cut 2 reported 3.042 s in and every cache warmed up again 1.012 s after the thaw; an interest another listener wrote after the second thaw reached this listener's cache 1 ms later; and no ERROR line anywhere in the process's output, start included. So the second cut ends as the first does.
proof.negativeControl: Two, and they answer different questions. (1) The guard's no-ERROR assertion is live: one `slog.Error` added to rewatchListenerKVWatchers in cmd/listener/main.go, which the cut path runs, makes it fail — `a silent cut and its rewatch logged an error: ... ERROR tester control: rewatching a cache cache=interest`. (2) The guard does not reach the replaced-watch branch: with kvwatch.Start's replaced-watch line forced from INFO to ERROR, the guard still passes, which is why the unit test above is the pin for roll call 5 and why the implementer's entry says so. Both patches were reverted with `jj restore`.

proof.criterion: The listener notices a dead hub in seconds (the spec's `Also in the second pull request` acceptance): a test stops answering the listener's pings without closing its socket, and the listener reports the connection lost within 5 seconds.
proof.surface: The real envoy-listener binary with the live lane on, against an in-process NATS whose relay stops moving bytes with both sides' connections kept (testnats.Server.Freeze).
proof.observed: 3 of 3 passed (ok 15.798s). `envoy` reported the cut 2.806 s, 2.837 s and 2.787 s after the freeze; `envoy-live-topics` 2.856 s, 2.837 s and 2.838 s. Every run is inside the 5 s the acceptance asks for.
proof.negativeControl: `bus.WithSilentCutDetection()` removed from openLiveTopics alone, at this head, with the test file untouched: `--- FAIL ... no disconnect line for envoy-live-topics 5.019s into a silent cut`, with `envoy`'s `nats: stale connection` line present, so the test pins each call site on its own. The same break of listenerStreamOptions failed naming `envoy` only in round 1, at code head 725e26a83afa, where that file is byte for byte what it is here. live_topics.go was restored with `jj restore`.

proof.criterion: The daemon notices a dead hub in seconds (the INFRA-14 architect's decision of 2026-10-30): the same ping settings at the daemon's one NATS connection, with a frozen-server test inside the same bound.
proof.surface: The daemon's own natsauth.Connect, called as internal/daemon/workflow.go:366 calls it (LogEvents and ReconnectForever), against a server that answers the handshake PING and then answers nothing with the socket open.
proof.observed: 2 of 2 passed under -race (ok 7.080s): the cut was noticed 3.011342769 s and 3.014144001 s after the server went quiet, with `NATS connection lost` logged and IsConnected false.
proof.negativeControl: `options = append(options, detectSilentCuts)` removed from Connect, at this head, the test file untouched: `--- FAIL ... the connection was not reported lost within 5.010558966s of the server going quiet: IsConnected = true, the warning logged = false`. natsauth.go was restored with `jj restore`.

roundOneFailureClosed.failure: Round 1 failed because the head carried no CI: that push ended on a handoff commit holding `skip-checks: true` while also carrying seven code commits, so GitHub started no run.
roundOneFailureClosed.readAtThisHead: Fixed. `gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/commits/b41bf83ff20f13ae967537e4b7952e56548a810b/check-runs` answers 2 at 08:00Z, `changes` and `pr-title`, both queued, where the same call answered 0 at every head of round 1. The head's commit message carries no `skip-checks` line (`jj log -r b41bf83f -T description | cat -A` ends at the `Omp-Session` trailer). A lane that is queued or running is read as such and waited for by nobody here; the required checks will settle on this head, and a red one sends the issue back without my completion.
roundOneFailureClosed.notRewritten: The implementer left the two already-pushed trailered commits as they are and says why in its handoff. That is right: what starts a run is the push, and this push started one.

environment: This pod has no container runtime, so the cmd/listener tests that start a Postgres container and the natsauth tests that need an authorized-server container are skipped by name or fail on `rootless Docker not found`, as the implementer records. Everything in this handoff ran without either.
No nats-server of this round was left running: every test above uses an in-process server from internal/testnats.
alsoChecked: The claim in kvwatch.Start's new doc comment that `the end of a replaced watcher is silent on the other path too (consume)` holds: consume guards its warm-up log, its scanEnded and its readiness release with `current := w.current(generation)` (internal/kvwatch/kvwatch.go:700, 717, 722), so a replaced generation writes nothing there.

The new code keeps the live-watch behaviour whole: a failed first start with no replacement still records w.err and still releases readiness, and the stopped case is unchanged, so Err(), Ping(), /healthz and the self-health rebuild read what they read before.

Acceptance 6's `The new text names no Dispatch key`: every added line of this round's diff outside .legion/INFRA-750/ holds no INFRA-, LEGION- or dispatch:// text; the new fragment packages/envoy/.changes/unreleased/pr-2542-replaced-watch-no-error.yaml carries `Issue: pr2542`.

The tester's round-1 observation is answered and its attribution corrected by the implementer: the two ERROR lines came from the test process's own second registry, whose connection the test closes while its first watches are live. Those watches are the live ones, so they keep their ERROR, which is what the architect's decision asks for; the branch the decision quiets is the replaced one, pinned by the unit test above.
